c01-p01.t: Mari Ríos had a big box, a roll of silver tape, and a very big idea.
I am going to be an astronaut for Halloween,
She cut a round hole in the box.
She cut two small holes for air.
She put silver tape on every side until the box was shiny.
Pepper sat on a chair and watched.
Pepper was a small black cat with big yellow eyes.
Pepper did not like the sound the scissors made.
Pepper jumped off the chair and hid under the table.

c01-p02.t: Mari put the box on her head.
She looked in the mirror by the door.
The helmet was a little bit too big.
One side was more silver than the other side.
But it was still the best helmet Mari had ever seen.
Mari said in her best astronaut voice.
Pepper peeked out from under the table.
Halloween was only one week away.
There were paper bats on the windows.
There were orange lights on the porch.
There was a big bowl for candy by the door, and it was empty, but not for long.

c01-p03.t: Mari's grandmother lived with Mari and her family.
Abuela had a garden behind the house.
In the summer, the garden was full of green vines.
Now, in October, the vines were brown, and the garden was full of pumpkins.
Some pumpkins were small, like a ball.
Some pumpkins were big, like a chair.
One pumpkin was so big that Mari could sit on it.
She was in the kitchen, making tea.
Do you know what real astronauts look at?

c01-p04.t: Mari and Abuela sat on the back steps.
It smelled like leaves and like Abuela's cinnamon tea.
The sky was dark blue, and it was full of stars.
When I was a little girl in Mexico,
my abuela told me that every star has a name.
Some stars are big and hot, like our sun.
Some are so far away that their light takes years and years to get here.
But space is very, very big.
She tried to think about something so big.
It made her head feel funny, in a good way.

c01-p05.t: The moon was up over the trees.
It was almost round, like a cookie with a little bite gone.
Every night, it gets a little rounder.
On Halloween night, it will be a full moon.
That is the best kind of Halloween.
The moon does not make its own light.
Abuela said the sun shines on it, like a flashlight on a ball.
The moon looks different every night because we see a different part of the sunny side.
She wanted to tell her teacher.

c01-p06.t: A light was moving across the sky.
It was not white like a star.
It was green, a bright, bright green, like a glow stick.
It made a long line, and then it curved down, down, down.
It went down past the trees.
It went down past the fence.
It went down right into Abuela's pumpkin patch.
There was a soft sound, like a pillow falling on the floor.
Abuela was looking at her tea.

c01-p07.t: The garden looked the same as always.
Nothing was green, and nothing was glowing.
Maybe it was a shooting star,
Shooting stars are little rocks from space.
They burn up very high in the sky.
They almost never come down to the ground.
Now, it is time for bed, little astronaut.
But she did not sleep for a long time.
She kept looking out her window at the dark garden.

c01-p08.t: In the morning, Mari put on her rain boots.
She put on her helmet, just in case.
Then she ran out to the garden.
Pepper came too, but slowly, and she stayed far behind.
It was a soft, humming sound.
Like a bee that was very, very sleepy.
It came from one big pumpkin by the fence.
This pumpkin was rounder than the others, and smoother, and very, very orange.

c01-p09.t: Mari put her ear on the pumpkin.
She put her hand on the pumpkin.
Not hot, just warm, like a cup of cocoa that was ready to drink.
Pepper hid behind the watering can.
Only her yellow eyes were showing.
There was a thin line all the way around the middle of the pumpkin, like the line on a lunch box.
And on the top, the stem was not brown.

c01-p10.t: She felt a little bit silly, talking to a pumpkin.
I guess you are just a pumpkin.
She turned to go back to the house.
Then, behind her, a tiny light came on.
Right on the side of the pumpkin, a small round window glowed green.
It went bright, and then dark, and then bright again.
And it was blinking right at Mari.

c02-p01.t: Her knees felt like jelly, and her heart went bump, bump, bump.
But she did not run away.
That is what Mari always said when something was new.
She walked back to the pumpkin.
Then there was a sound like a soda can opening.
The line around the middle of the pumpkin got wider.
The top half of the pumpkin lifted up, slowly, like a lid on a pot.
A puff of mist came out.
It smelled like oranges and peppermint.
Pepper made a sound like a squeaky toy and ran into the garage.

c02-p02.t: Something peeked over the edge of the pumpkin.
It was about as big as a cat.
It was a soft purple color, like a grape, and it was a little bit shiny.
They were dark and sparkly, like the night sky.
On top of its head were three thin antennae.
Each one wobbled like a spring, and each one had a tiny light on the end.
The little creature looked at Mari.
Mari looked at the little creature.
Then the creature floated up, out of the pumpkin.
It just floated, a little bit above the ground, and bobbed up and down like a balloon.

c02-p03.t: It looked at Mari's rain boots.
Then it looked up at her shiny silver helmet.
Its antennae lit up bright blue.
Its voice was high and bubbly, like a bird and a kazoo at the same time.
I learn your words from the radio.
Many songs about love and also about cars.

c02-p04.t: The creature bowed in the air.
It turned all the way upside down and then right side up.
On the radio, everybody says it.
I'll tell you about it later.
said Mari, and she pushed her helmet up so she could see better.
I am not really an astronaut.
I made it out of a box.

c02-p05.t: Zib floated around Mari in a circle.
It looked at the helmet very closely.
It tapped the silver tape with one tiny purple hand.
You make a space helmet from a box.
Mari felt her cheeks get warm.
Nobody had ever called her a very smart human-friend before.
Zib pointed up, past the trees, past the clouds.
A purple planet with green rings.
Just then, Pepper came out of the garage.
Pepper jumped straight up in the air.
Then she ran and hid inside one of Dad's rain boots.
Only her tail was sticking out.

c02-p06.t: The tail in the boot went swish, swish.
Mari thought that was probably a hello.
Then Zib floated back to the pumpkin.
It looked inside, and its antennae turned a sad gray color.
Mari looked inside the pumpkin too.
It was not full of seeds and goo, like a real pumpkin.
It had a little seat, and buttons, and a round glass jar in the middle.
The jar had eight small holes in it, like an egg box.

c02-p07.t: They are like… like batteries, but shiny.
They make the ship go zoom.
Zib made a sound like a sigh.
When I land, I land too fast.
The jar opens, and the glow-seeds fly out.
And there is one more problem.
Zib pointed up at the sky again.
In the morning light, Mari could just see the moon, pale and white, like a ghost of the moon.
My ship can only fly home when the moon is round and full,
A road of light, all the way home.

c02-p08.t: Mari thought about what Abuela had said last night.
The full moon is on Halloween!
If I find all eight glow-seeds in seven days, I go home on Halloween night.
My mama and my papa and my little brother will be so happy.
And if you don't find them?
One whole year, for the next good moon.
But I will miss them very much.
Mari thought about missing Abuela, and Mom and Dad, and even Pepper, for a whole year.
It made her tummy feel sad and heavy.

c02-p09.t: I will help you find your glow-seeds.
Zib's antennae lit up like a rainbow.
Red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple, all at once.
You are the most real astronaut I know.
You are the only astronaut I know.
Its three antennae stood straight up, like the ears of a dog that hears a cookie bag.
The lights on the ends of the antennae turned yellow.
And all three of them pointed the same way, across the yard, over the fence, down the street.

c02-p10.t: My antennae can feel them when they are close-ish.
Mari looked where the antennae were pointing.
Past the big oak tree on the corner.
She walked that way every single morning with her backpack.
That's the way to my school,
Just then, from inside the house, Mom called out,
And put on your clothes, mija, or you'll be late for school!
how do you feel about backpacks?

c03-p01.t: It is like a little house,
A little house with a zipper door.
And there is a banana in here!
I only say hello to it,
Mari walked to school with Mom.
The backpack was a little bit heavy, and once in a while it hummed.
Mom was talking about the costume parade.
I can't believe it's Costume Day already,
She held up the silver box.

c03-p02.t: At Willow Creek Elementary, every class was ready for the Fall Costume Parade.
After lunch, all the kids would walk around the playground in their costumes.
All the families would come to watch and clap.
Mari's teacher, Ms. Patel, had a big pumpkin on her desk.
She said the pumpkin would get a prize ribbon for the best costume, after the parade.
Mari hung her backpack on her hook.
[whispering] I am very good at staying.
The backpack's three antennae poked out of the top, glowing yellow.

c03-p03.t: All morning, Mari tried to do her work.
Ms. Patel was teaching about leaves.
In the fall, she said, trees stop making the green stuff that they use to eat sunlight.
When the green goes away, you can see the yellow and orange that were hiding there all along.
So the leaves aren't turning orange,
They were orange the whole time?
The green was just on top.
Mari thought that was very cool.
But when she looked at her hook, her backpack was open.

c03-p04.t: She looked in the reading corner.
She looked behind the big plant by the window.
A high, bubbly giggle, like a bird and a kazoo.
It came from the back of the room, where the class kept the costume box.
The box was full of old hats and capes and masks for dress-up time.
On top of the box sat a pirate hat.
Under the pirate hat was a purple face with two big sparkly eyes.

c03-p05.t: Mari ran over and picked up Zib.
She was just about to put it back in the backpack, when the bell rang.
All the kids got in a line.
She had her helmet in one hand.
She had Zib in the other hand.
And you made a little alien friend too!
Mari did not know what to say.

c03-p06.t: The parade was so much fun.
There was a dinosaur and a fairy.
There was a hot dog and a robot and two pirates.
There was a girl dressed as a bunch of grapes, with purple balloons all over her shirt.
It floated a little higher off Mari's shoulder.
Its antennae flashed every color, one after the other, like a light show.
How does she make it float?
Her heart was going fast, but it was a happy kind of fast now.

c03-p07.t: After the parade, everybody went back inside.
Ms. Patel stood next to the big pumpkin on her desk.
She held up a shiny blue ribbon.
But the ribbon for the Most Creative Costume goes to… Mari and her alien friend!
But when Zib got close to the big pumpkin, its antennae stopped flashing.
All three of them pointed right at the pumpkin on Ms. Patel's desk.

c03-p08.t: The top had been cut off and put back on, like a little hat.
Ms. Patel was going to carve a face on it later.
can I look inside the pumpkin?
Inside were the seeds, flat and white and slimy.
And there, right in the middle, was one seed that was not flat, or white, or slimy.
It was round, like a marble.
Mari reached in and picked it up.
It felt warm, and a little bit tingly, like the feeling when your foot is waking up.

c03-p09.t: That afternoon, after school, Mari ran to the garden.
Zib floated next to her as fast as it could go.
Mari put the glowing seed into the glass jar inside the pumpkin-ship.
It fit into the first hole perfectly.
The ship hummed a little louder.
One of the round buttons turned green.
It did a happy flip in the air.
She hung the blue ribbon on the pumpkin's silver stem.

c03-p10.t: Its antennae stood up, straight and tall.
The little lights turned yellow, and they pointed.
Past the house with the big plastic spider on the roof.
They pointed all the way to the end of Maple Street.
To an old, tall house, with dark windows and twisty vines all over the walls.
There was a strange metal thing on the roof, like a giant tube.
The yard was full of tall weeds and stone statues.
Every kid on Maple Street knew about that house.
Every kid on Maple Street said the same thing about it.
said Mari in a very small voice,
that's the house where the witch lives.

c04-p01.t: Mari and Zib were sitting on the back steps.
Pepper was sitting far away, on top of the fence, watching Zib with big round eyes.
A witch is… well, it's a pretend thing,
In stories, a witch has a pointy hat and a broom, and she flies on the broom, and she makes potions in a big pot.
Sometimes witches in stories are mean.
And there is one in the house at the end of the street?
She never comes to the block party.
She has a big hat, and she walks around her yard at night, and there's a weird metal tube on her roof.

c04-p02.t: Zib floated up in front of Mari's face.
So you do not know if she is mean.
It means a thing you are scared of, because you do not know it yet.
She thought about how scared Pepper was of Zib.
Pepper thought Zib was a blorp.
But Zib was the nicest, silliest blorp in the whole world.
Maybe Mrs. Crump is a blorp,

c04-p03.t: Mari was not allowed to go to a house by herself, and she did not want to.
I have wanted to meet her for a long time.
I see her light on very late at night.
Let's bring her some pan dulce.
So Abuela put six sweet breads in a basket and covered them with a pretty cloth.
Mari put Zib in her backpack.
I am a very good stayer,
You stayed for about one minute today.
That is very good for me,

c04-p04.t: The sun was going down, and the sky was turning orange and pink.
The houses on Maple Street all had Halloween decorations.
The yellow house had a scarecrow.
The blue house had a ghost made from a sheet.
The house with the big plastic spider had a sign that said
The spider had a party hat on.
Then they came to the very last house.
Up close, the house was old and tall.
Thick red vines climbed all over the walls.
The yard had tall, waving grasses and stone statues of rabbits and owls.
On the roof, there was a round dome, like a little metal hat, with a long brass tube poking out.
Mari held Abuela's hand a little tighter.

c04-p05.t: Abuela knocked on the door.
Knock, knock, knock.
For a long time, nothing happened.
Then they heard footsteps.
Slow, heavy footsteps.
Clomp.
Clomp.
Clomp.
The door creaked open.
A tall woman stood there.
She had silver hair in a long braid.
She had a very big, very floppy black hat.
She had little round glasses, and she was frowning.
Yes?
she said, in a deep voice.
Mari wanted to hide behind Abuela.
Maybe in a rain boot, like Pepper.
But Abuela just smiled her big smile.
Good evening!
I am Lupe Ríos, from the white house with the pumpkins.
And this is my granddaughter, Mari.
We brought you some pan dulce.

c04-p06.t: The woman looked at the basket.
In its place came a smile so big that her glasses went up on her cheeks.
I'm so sorry about my grumpy face.
I was up all night, and I'm only half awake.
Mrs. Crump did not sound like a witch at all.
Why were you up all night?
Mrs. Crump's eyes twinkled behind her glasses.
Because, my dear, that's when the stars come out.

c04-p07.t: Mrs. Crump's house was not scary inside.
It was warm and messy and wonderful.
Books on the shelves, books on the chairs, books on the stairs.
There were maps of the stars on the walls.
There were pictures of the moon, big and gray and bumpy, with little circles all over it.
Holes, where space rocks hit the moon a long, long time ago.

c04-p08.t: Mrs. Crump took them up the stairs to a round room at the very top of the house.
The roof of this room could open up, like a window to the sky.
In the middle stood a huge brass telescope.
That's the tube on your roof!
I was a star scientist for forty years.
I still look at the sky every night.
I'm not a very good sleeper, but I'm a very good looker.

c04-p09.t: A telescope works like a giant eye,
It catches lots and lots of light from far away.
Then it makes the light small and bright, so it fits in your eye.
That's how we can see things that are very far away.
Abuela was looking at a picture of Saturn, with its big beautiful rings.
Mrs. Crump leaned down close to Mari.
last night I saw something very strange in my telescope.
It came down from the sky, and I think it landed near your house.
Mari's heart went bump, bump, bump.

c04-p10.t: Zib floated out of the backpack.
It bobbed in the air, right in front of Mrs. Crump's round glasses.
She cleaned them on her sweater.
Forty years of looking at the sky.
And the sky came to look at me.
But Abuela was across the room, with her back to them.
She was reading a book about the moon, and humming a song.
I'm very good at being quiet and watching.
Your secret is safe with me.

c04-p11.t: They pointed out the window, down into the yard.
They all went down to the yard, Abuela too.
Let's look at your garden before it gets too dark,
In the middle of the yard stood a stone bird bath, shaped like a big flower.
The water inside was glowing green.
There, at the bottom of the water, was a round, shiny glow-seed.
whispered Mari, and she picked it up.
said Abuela, who could not see Zib.
said Mrs. Crump, and winked at Mari.

c04-p12.t: When it was time to go, Mrs. Crump walked them to the gate.
everybody on our street thinks you're a witch.
Mrs. Crump laughed a big laugh.
Well, I do love a big hat.
And I'm a bit grumpy before my coffee.
I suppose I can see why.
Something you're scared of only because it's new,

Out where the corn grows tall.
Mari and Zib looked at each other.
It has a giant corn maze.

c05-p01.t: On Saturday, the whole family went to Harvest Hill Farm.
Abuela brought a big bag of oranges.
Mari brought her backpack, and her backpack brought Zib.
[whispering] On my planet, we grow food in tall glass towers.
The farm was big and busy.
There was a red barn and a pile of pumpkins as tall as a car.
There was a wagon full of hay, pulled by a green tractor.
Kids sat on the hay and bounced and laughed.
And at the end of the farm, there was a field of corn taller than Dad.

c05-p02.t: A sign at the start had a big map.
The paths in the corn twisted and turned like spaghetti.
This maze is shaped like a giant bat,
From an airplane, you can see its wings.
Mari and Dad went in together.
Zib floated low, between them, close to the ground, where the corn leaves hid it.
The corn went shhh, shhh in the wind.
At the first corner, they turned right.
At the next corner, they turned left.
Then they came to a dead end.

c05-p03.t: They wiggled one way, then the other.
But the corn is in the way.
Ms. Patel had taught them a maze trick.
if you put one hand on the wall and never let go, you will get out of almost any maze.
It might take a long time.
But you won't get lost forever.
So Mari put her right hand on the corn.
She walked, and walked, and turned every time the wall turned.

c05-p04.t: They passed a sign that said
They passed the same yellow flower two times.

Then the scarecrow started to laugh.

c05-p05.t: The scarecrow took off its pumpkin head.
It was not a scarecrow at all.
It was a man with a gray beard and a big smile.
I sit here every Saturday to surprise people.
It's my favorite part of the whole year.
Mari laughed so hard she had to sit on the hay.
And what a great alien costume, young lady.
Farmer Joe held out his basket.
Take an apple for the road.
And one round, bright, lime-green thing that was not an apple at all.

c05-p06.t: I found it in the corn on Thursday.
I thought it was some kind of toy.
Mari held the glow-seed in her hand.
Zib whispered back, and its antennae turned pink.
Then Mari put her right hand back on the corn wall, and they walked, and walked, and turned.
And at last, they came out of the bat's left wing, right next to the barn, where Mom and Abuela were waiting with apple cider.

c05-p07.t: That night, Mari put the third glow-seed into the jar.

It sounded like the kind of song you sing when you miss somebody.
Zib floated very still beside the ship.
It is singing a home song.
It sings it when it is far from home for too long.

She listened to the sad, soft song.

c06-p01.t: The kitchen light was Abuela, making a late cup of tea.

She yawned and went to bed.
Mari let out a big breath.
But on Sunday morning, Abuela came down to the kitchen very early.
And there, on the counter, was a small purple alien with its whole face in the sugar jar.

c06-p02.t: She ran down the stairs in her pajamas.

When I was a little girl, my grandmother told me that the stars sometimes send visitors.
I always hoped I would meet one.

c06-p03.t: Abuela listened to the whole story.
And how many have you found?
Zib pointed one tiny finger at the sugar jar.
That is why I was in there.

c06-p04.t: Down, down, down, to the very bottom of the jar.
Round and warm and glowing green, with sugar sticking to it like snow.

c06-p06.t: It turned pink, then orange, then yellow, then green, then blue, like a rainbow moving from its head down to its belly.
This is the best food in the whole universe.
Abuela laughed and gave Zib another piece.

But the animals of the forest helped it.
The owl showed it the way, and the rabbit kept it warm.
And on the clearest night of the year, the little star floated back up to its family.
That is why we help each other find the way.

c06-p07.t: Zib floated over and gave Abuela a small, sticky hug around her neck.
In this house, there is always room for one more.
After breakfast, Mari and Zib ran out to the garden.

And only five more days until the moon is full.

c07-p01.t: On Monday night, the town library had a special party.

Kids came in pajamas and costumes.
There were paper pumpkins on the shelves and orange lights around the windows.

[whispering] a library is a quiet place.

Mari went to the space books.

It is purple, with green rings.

c07-p04.t: Then she remembered something Mrs. Crump had said.
Zib, these are only the planets that go around our sun,

So my planet goes around a different star?
A star so far away, it looks tiny from here.

One of those is my sun,
Then its antennae turned pink again.
That is a nice thing to know.

c07-p05.t: Zib spun around in the air.

And in the gym, there was the Haunted House that the fifth graders had built.
Mari stood at the door with Mom.
The sign said HAUNTED HOUSE in big, drippy, green letters.
Behind the door, she could hear spooky music.
Mari's knees felt like jelly again.
You don't have to go in,
Zib's antennae were bright, bright yellow.

c08-p02.t: Just then, somebody tapped Mari on the shoulder.
It was Leo, her best friend from class.
He had a knight costume with a cardboard shield.
Mom, can Leo and I go in together?
I'll be right here at the exit.
And from inside Mom's big tote bag, where nobody had noticed her, a small black cat jumped out and followed them.

c08-p03.t: The Haunted House was dark, but not too dark.
Purple lights glowed on the cardboard walls.
There were paper bats hanging from strings, and cotton cobwebs in every corner.
A ghost swung down from the ceiling.
With two eyes drawn on with a marker.
A skeleton sat in a chair.
It was made of plastic, and when they walked by, it started to sing a song about bones in a silly, wobbly voice.

c08-p04.t: Then they heard a sound behind them.
She was standing in the middle of the path, with her fur all puffed up like a dandelion.
Her tail was as big as a bottle brush.
In front of Pepper was a mop.
A big gray mop with long, floppy strings, leaning on the wall.
The mop still did not move.
Pepper jumped straight up in the air, turned around and ran right into Mari's backpack.
And out of the backpack, with a black cat now sitting where it used to be, floated Zib.

c08-p05.t: Zib is from another planet, and Zib is my friend, and Zib needs our help, and it's a secret.
He held up his cardboard shield, like a real knight making a promise.
You are a very good human-friend too,

c08-p06.t: Mari told Leo about the glow-seeds as fast as she could.
Leo listened with his eyes wide.
They pointed to the very last room of the Haunted House.
Thick, white fog was rolling out from under the door.
The last room had a big black pot, like a witch's cauldron, made from a trash can.
The fog was coming out of a little machine hidden behind it.
The machine was going pfff, pfff, pfff.
And every time it puffed, the fog glowed a little bit green.

c08-p07.t: It's stuck in the fog machine!
said Leo.
Mari looked closer.
A glow-seed was stuck right in the hole where the fog came out.
Mari did not touch the machine.
That was a rule.
You don't touch machines that you don't know.
Instead, she found one of the fifth graders who was helping.
Her name was Jada, and she was dressed like a friendly vampire.
Excuse me,
said Mari,
I think something is stuck in your fog machine.
Jada turned off the machine and looked.
Huh!
A marble!
She pulled out the glow-seed and gave it to Mari.
Thanks for telling me.
It was going to break.
[whispering] Six,
whispered Mari, and put it in her pocket.

c08-p08.t: When they came out of the Haunted House, Zib was hiding behind Leo's big cardboard shield.
Mom was waiting at the exit.
She was holding her empty tote bag and looking very confused.
Mari,
said Mom,
why is the cat in your backpack?
It's a long story,
said Mari.
Leo walked them to the car.
Before they said goodbye, he whispered,
[whispering] Tomorrow, I want to help find the last two seeds.
Then a big, cold drop of water fell on Mari's nose.
Then another.
Then lots and lots of them.
It started to rain.
Hard.
All the way home, Zib sat in Mari's lap, looking out the car window at the rain.
It did not say
hello-treat.
It did not say anything.
Its antennae had turned gray, and they did not turn any other color for the whole ride home.

c09-p01.t: On Wednesday, it rained all day.
It rained on the paper bats on the windows.
It rained so much that the street looked like a little river.
There was no school that afternoon, because the teachers had a meeting.
Zib floated by the window, watching the rain.
Mari tried to cheer it up.
She showed Zib how to make a paper airplane.
She showed Zib how to build a pillow fort.
She showed Zib her favorite cartoon.
But it said it in a small, quiet voice.

c09-p02.t: At last, Mari sat down next to Zib on the window seat.
Zib was quiet for a long time.
Rain went tap, tap, tap on the glass.
On my planet, when it rains, my mama makes warm soup.
My little brother, Zub, jumps in the puddles and gets all wet.
Mari felt her own eyes get a little wet.
She thought about how she would feel if she were very far away from Mom and Dad and Abuela.

c09-p03.t: Abuela always said that sad feelings are like rain.
You can't make them stop by yelling at them.
You just wait with them, and keep each other company, until they pass.
So Mari just sat next to Zib.
She put a blanket over both of them.
Pepper came over and curled up on Mari's feet, which she almost never did when Zib was around.
A tiny bit of pink came back to one antenna.
He is very small and very loud.

c09-p04.t: In the evening, the rain stopped.
The clouds started to break apart.
She says that after a big rain, the air is very clean.
It is the best night to look at the stars.
So Mari, Abuela and Zib walked down Maple Street.
The sidewalk was shiny and wet.
The street lights made yellow puddles.
Mrs. Crump was waiting at her door with a lantern.

c09-p05.t: In the round room at the top of the house, the roof was open.
The sky was black and clear, and full of stars.
Mrs. Crump turned the big brass telescope.
She looked through it, and turned some knobs, and looked again.
can you tell me what your sun looks like from here?
Zib floated up to the window.
It looked at the stars for a long time.
Those three stars in a line, like a belt.
And then up, up, a little to the left.

c09-p06.t: Zib put its big eye to the telescope.
And in the telescope, small and bright and orange, was a star.
I'm afraid we can't see your planet,
Planets around other stars are very small and very dim.
Even the biggest telescopes on Earth can almost never see them.
But your sun is right there.
And your planet is right next to it, going around and around.
Zib did not move from the telescope for a long time.
Then, slowly, its antennae began to change.
Gray, then light gray, then a soft blue.
Right there, next to that little orange light.
Maybe my mama is looking at the sky right now too.

c09-p07.t: Mari hugged Zib, very carefully, because Zib was soft and round and hard to hug.
We're going to get you home,
Just like Leo promised on his shield.
On the walk home, the stars were bright over Maple Street.
Zib floated between Mari and Abuela, and for the first time in two days, it hummed a little song.

c09-p08.t: Then, just as they got to their front gate, Zib stopped.
All three antennae shot straight up.
Then they turned yellow again, even brighter, two times, blink, blink.
They are right here, on our street.
Like somebody is carrying them from place to place.
Mari looked at all the houses on Maple Street, with their pumpkins and their ghosts and their big plastic spiders.
in two more days, every house on this street will open its door.
And every kid in town will knock on it.

c10-p01.t: Mari put on her white hoodie with the stars and planets.
She put on her shiny silver helmet.
It still wobbled a little, but that was okay.
Leo came over in his knight costume, with his cardboard shield.
Pepper had tiny purple bat wings on her back, which Mom had made out of felt.
Pepper did not love the wings.
But she did not take them off, either.
Abuela laughed and gave Zib a little orange bucket.
Then you are the best-dressed Zib in town.

c10-p02.t: Dad came too, with a flashlight.
The sky was pink and purple.
And over the trees, the moon was rising.
It was big and round and orange, like a giant pumpkin in the sky.
Down Maple Street, all the porch lights were on.
There were witches and pirates and dinosaurs and one very tall banana.

c10-p03.t: At the first house, Mari knocked on the door.
She held a bowl of candy.
The lady laughed and put a candy in each bucket, even Zib's.
Zib looked at the candy in its bucket.
It is a… a door game.
You knock, and people are kind to you, and you say thank you.
Zib turned back to the lady.
it said, and bowed upside down.

c10-p04.t: They went from house to house.
The yellow house had a scarecrow.
The blue house had a sheet ghost.
But the glow-seeds were hard to find.
Then Leo pointed down the sidewalk.
A little boy, about three years old, was walking with his dad.
He was dressed as a pumpkin.
And in his hand, he was holding something round and glowing green.
Zib's antennae went so bright yellow they almost looked white.

c10-p05.t: Mari walked over and knelt down.
she said to the little boy.
She had a big chocolate bar.
The biggest one she had gotten all night.
The little boy looked at the chocolate.
He looked at the glowing ball.
He looked at the chocolate again.
He's been carrying it around all week.

c10-p06.t: There was only one seed left.
Zib's antennae pointed to the house with the big plastic spider on the roof.
The spider still had its party hat on.
The man who lived there, Mr. Lee, was sitting on the porch.
Next to him was a giant bowl of candy.
And on top of the candy, right in the middle, sat a round green light.
I found this in my gutter on Monday,
I thought it made a nice decoration for my candy bowl.
could I please have the green one, instead of candy?
Then he gave her two candies anyway.

c10-p07.t: said Mari, and Leo, and Zib, all at the same time.
Walked, actually, because Dad said walk.
But they walked very, very fast.
In the garden, Mari opened the pumpkin-ship.
She put the seventh seed in the jar.
She put the eighth seed in the jar.
Then the pumpkin-ship started to glow.
Then so much that the whole garden turned green, like they were standing under the sea.
And it's almost time for Zib to go home.
Above them, the full moon was high and bright.
And from the moon, all the way down to the pumpkin-ship, a thin silver line of light began to shine, like a road.

c11-p01.t: Soon, everybody was in the garden.
Mom came out in her slippers.
Abuela came out with a pot of hot cocoa.
Leo's mom came to pick him up, saw the glowing pumpkin, and stayed.
And Mrs. Crump came down Maple Street as fast as she could, holding her lantern and her big floppy hat.
I saw the light from my roof!
she said, out of breath.
Is it time?
It's time,
said Zib.
Everybody stood in a circle around the pumpkin-ship.
It hummed.
It glowed.
The silver road of moonlight shone down on it from the sky.
Nobody was scared.
Not even Mom.
Well, maybe a little bit, at first.
But then Zib floated over and said,
Hello-treat, Mari's mama,
and Mom laughed and said hello back.

c11-p02.t: Mrs. Crump put down her lantern.
She took out a little notebook and a pencil.
She looked at the moon.
She looked at the ship.
She wrote numbers in her notebook.
Zib,
she said,
the moon road will be strongest when the moon is highest in the sky.
That will be in about ten minutes.
You'll want to go straight up, and then follow the light.
Ten minutes,
said Zib.
You are a very smart star-lady.
Mrs. Crump smiled so big that her glasses went up on her cheeks.
Zib floated into the pumpkin-ship.
It sat in the tiny seat.
It pushed some buttons.
The ship hummed louder and louder.
Then, suddenly, the ship gave a big shake.
BUMP!

c11-p03.t: The jar in the middle of the ship rattled.
And one glow-seed popped right out of its hole.
It bounced off the edge of the pumpkin.
Then it rolled away, under the big brown leaves, deep into the darkest corner of the garden, way back by the fence.
[excited] The ship cannot go with only seven!
But the corner was thick with vines and old pumpkins, and the seed was hiding under all of it.
said Mrs. Crump, looking at her watch.

c11-p04.t: Then something small and black moved through the grass.
Pepper, who was scared of boxes, and tape, and scissors.
Pepper, who was scared of mops, and flips, and flying sugar.
Pepper, who had hidden in a rain boot the very first time she saw Zib.
Pepper walked to the edge of the dark vines.

c11-p05.t: For a few seconds, nobody could see her.
Somebody's breath went in and did not come out.
And out came Pepper, walking very proudly, with her tail straight up in the air.
In her mouth, held very gently, like a mother cat carries a kitten, was a small, round, glowing glow-seed.
She walked right up to the pumpkin-ship.
And she dropped the glow-seed at Zib's feet.
Well, at the place where Zib's feet would be, if Zib had feet.

c11-p06.t: She scooped up the cat and hugged her.
Zib put the glow-seed back in the jar.
All eight buttons were green again.
This time, Zib pushed the jar's lid closed, tight.
Mrs. Crump threw her big hat in the air, and Dad had to catch it.
said Mrs. Crump, a little out of breath from cheering.

c11-p07.t: It floated up, slowly, one inch above the ground.
Its light turned from green to gold.
But just before the lid came down, Zib floated back out.
It looked at her with its big, sparkly eyes.
Its antennae were glowing a color Mari had never seen before.
It was a soft color, somewhere between pink and gold.
before I go, I have something for you.
She felt a lump in her throat.
said Zib, and it held out one tiny purple hand.

c12-p01.t: In Zib's tiny hand was a seed.
It was smaller, and flatter, and shaped like a little teardrop.
It looked almost like a pumpkin seed.
But it was purple, and it had a soft, tiny glow, like a night-light.
On my planet, when you make a very good friend, you give them a friend-seed.
Then, wherever they are, they have a little piece of you.
Zib put the friend-seed in it.
It was warm, like a hug.

c12-p02.t: Then Zib floated to everybody, one by one.
It hugged Abuela around the neck.
Thank you for the candied pumpkin, big Abuela.
And for the story about the little star.
Que te vaya bonito, little star,
said Abuela, and she wiped her eyes with her rebozo.
It bowed upside down to Mrs. Crump.
for coming to visit an old astronomer.
It gave Leo a high five on his shield.
She just reached up and touched her nose to Zib's nose.

c12-p03.t: Last of all, Zib floated back to Mari.
For a moment, neither of them said anything.
on my planet, they will ask me, 'Zib, what is Earth like?' Do you know what I will say?
I will say, Earth is a place where you fall down in the dark, and you are lost, and you are scared,
And then a girl in a box helmet comes and says, 'Let's find out.' And everybody helps.
Mari laughed, and cried a little, both at the same time.
Will I ever see you again?
Zib's antennae glowed pink and gold.
And the moon road comes back.

c12-p04.t: Up past the big oak tree.
Up, up, up, along the silver road of moonlight.
From the little round window, a tiny purple hand waved and waved.
Dad held up the flashlight and blinked it on and off, like a goodbye.
Higher and higher went the pumpkin-ship.
It got smaller, and smaller, until it looked like a little golden star.
Then, right in front of the moon, it stopped for one second.
It drew a long, bright green line across the sky.
The line curved up at both ends.
Then the little star went zip and was gone.

c12-p05.t: For a long time, everybody stood in the garden, looking up.
That was the best Halloween ever.
Abuela poured everybody a cup of hot cocoa.
Mrs. Crump told Leo's mom all about telescopes.
Leo told everybody, again, about the mop.
Pepper sat on Mari's feet and purred.
Mari held the friend-seed in her hand.
It glowed softly, like a tiny piece of the moon road.
She thought about Zib, flying past the moon, past the planets, past all the stars, toward one small orange sun.
Toward a mama making soup, and a papa telling jokes, and a little brother named Zub, jumping in puddles.

c12-p06.t: In the spring, Mari planted the friend-seed in Abuela's garden, right next to the pumpkins.
All summer long, she watered it.
A little vine grew.
It had leaves shaped like stars.
And the next October, in the middle of Abuela's pumpkin patch, there was a small round pumpkin.
It was not orange.
It was purple, with soft green stripes.
And at night, it glowed.
Mari was eight now.
She was working on a new Halloween costume.
It had a purple hat.
It had three springy antennae, made from pipe cleaners and ping-pong balls.
What are you going to be this year, mija?
asked Abuela.
Mari put on the hat.
She looked up at the sky, where the moon was getting rounder every night.
I'm going to be dressed as Zib,
said Mari.
So that when Zib comes back, it will know exactly where to find me.
THE END
